chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Abu Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from 'Ubaydillah ibn 'Ali al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Muhrim (person in Ihram), if he fears the enemy, wears armor, then there is no expiation (kaffarah) upon him.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pilgrim wearing armor if they fear an enemy attack?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of wearing stitched garments (or armor, depending on the fiqh interpretation of 'silah') is lifted when a pilgrim fears for their safety, establishing the principle of *darurah* (necessity) in Hajj rituals. It highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence, where the preservation of life overrides ritual restrictions, ensuring that the pilgrim is not burdened beyond their capacity during times of conflict.
